subject: ventures/wedding-videographer-profit-calculator
professional: the accountant or bookkeeper of a solo wedding-film studio (and the studio owner who prices packages): first checks that revenue, direct costs and owner hours add up to a true hourly rate and a minimum price that actually returns that rate when re-quoted, then asks what is missing between 'profit' and what the owner keeps (self-employment and income tax, unpaid admin, sales tax)

evidence.correctness: Imported calc.mjs and ran three bookings through calculateBooking, then recomputed each in a separate Python script written from the definitions (revenue = price + extra rounds x fee; hours = shoot + travel + prep + edits + rounds used x hours/round; costs = second shooter + travel + gear/bookings + delivery + processing % of revenue; minimum price = (target x hours + fixed costs)/(1 - processing) - extra-round revenue). (1) $4,200 full day, 10 h shoot, 10 h second shooter at $30, 19 edit h, 3 of 2 rounds at 2 h, $150 extra fee, target $60: tool 35 h, profit $4,050, $115.71/h, min price $2,250; Python and a hand sum (4,350 revenue - 300 second shooter = 4,050; 60x35 + 300 - 150 = 2,250) identical. (2) $3,000, 8 h shoot, 2 h travel, 3 h prep, 20 edit h, 5 of 2 rounds, $3,000 gear over 30 bookings, 3% processing: 43 h, profit $2,996.50, $69.69/h, min $2,127.32; Python identical. (3) $2,800, 2.9% processing, $2,400 gear over 24: 30 h, $2,603.80, $86.79/h, min $2,435.63; identical. The minimum-price round trip (re-quote at minPrice returns the target) is also tested. Caveat: the page itself was not loaded in a browser; wiring was checked by confirming every id read by index.html exists and by importing the same module. The 'profit' is pre-tax by design (see domain). Edge: processing 99% with target $50 returns a $25,000 minimum price, correct arithmetic but absurd input is accepted.
evidence.completeness: Checked each claim in README, VENTURE.yaml and the page: true hourly rate (works), profit per booking (works), minimum package price for a target (works), edit-hour sensitivity table at 75/100/125/150/200% (works), break-even edit hours (works, round-trip tested), deliverable ladder (works, 3 default tiers, add/remove in page JS), revision cap with extra-round fee (works), worked example button (PRESETS[2], wired), usage opt-out (usage.mjs, tested). All 27 element ids the page script reads exist. No TODO/FIXME in the files. Not covered, and not claimed: income tax, sales tax, live market rates. Not run in a browser.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/wedding-videographer-profit-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 23 tests, 23 pass, 0 fail, ~0.14 s (calc 10, page 7, usage 6). Seeded mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted with git checkout (git status clean): (a) gear cost divisor bookingsPerYear -> bookingsPerYear + 1 at line 78: caught (test 1 failed). (b) extra revision rounds minus an extra 1 at line 70: caught (test 2 failed). (c) edit-share warning boundary '>= 0.5' -> '> 0.5' at line 126: NOT caught, 23 of 23 still passed. So the money arithmetic is guarded but the boundary of a warning and most message text are not; there is no test of the headline-versus-true finding, the sensitivity minPrice values, or the ladder prices/profits (only hoursWorked of row 0 and best >= row 0). Page tests are string matches on the HTML, not behaviour: nothing executes the page script, so a broken DOM wiring would pass.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (169 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, and the module script in index.html. Good: pure functions, one validation helper, errors returned as {error}, no network, escaping helper in the page. Defects: (1) money() findings for revision hours use b.revisionHours.toFixed but the 'Revision creep' text says 'about N hours of revisions' while the number counts all rounds used, not only the extra ones, so the sentence misleads when 2 of 2 included rounds are used (calc.mjs:136); (2) deliverableLadder zeroes ceremony/speeches edit hours and replaces the highlight hours, so the user's own three edit fields are silently ignored in the ladder and tier price is the only link to the main form (calc.mjs:157); (3) canonical, sitemap and robots use relative URLs ('./index.html', 'Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml'), which crawlers do not accept (index.html canonical, sitemap.xml:3, robots.txt:3); (4) bookingsPerYear accepts 1.5 and processingPercent 99 with no sanity warning; (5) tier input errors blank the whole ladder but not the main report, with only a table cell message.
evidence.claims: Backed: 'entirely client-side, nothing uploaded' (page.test asserts no fetch/XMLHttpRequest in index.html and calc.mjs; usage.mjs stores counts locally, read); 'example presets are unverified approximations' (stated in calc.mjs, page and FAQ, tested); disclaimer and 'does not cover income tax, sales tax or contract terms' (FAQ text, tested to match visible copy); the true-rate and minimum-price claims (recomputed above). Not backed or stale: llms.txt links to duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/... not marisstella.app although CLAUDE.md says the old host only redirects; README gives the test command with a glob that Node 22 handles only in a shell and does not say 23 tests; the FAQ says total hours are 'commonly two to four times the shoot hours', an industry rule of thumb with no source and no file behind it (the preset itself is 35/10 = 3.5x, so it is self-consistent but unsourced); the hypothesis in VENTURE.yaml is 'untested' and stage is 'prototype', which is honest. README promises 'which used to mean guessing', a marketing claim nothing backs.
evidence.fitness: Walked a studio owner's job: load the example, change price to a real quote, set the second shooter, enter edit hours, read the true rate, see the minimum price for $50/h, try the three tiers. Each step produced a coherent answer in a few fields, and the sensitivity table is the genuinely useful part. What a real owner hits in the first hour: the 'true hourly rate' is before any income or self-employment tax so it overstates take-home by roughly a fifth to a third and is not labelled as pre-tax in the results table; no field for client meetings, album/proofing time, music licensing, backup storage or a travel-mileage rate (travel cost is a typed total); the target default $50 and gear $4,000 are arbitrary; no way to save or compare bookings; USD only; the 'Edit hours the booking can absorb' line is not explained next to the number.
evidence.domain: Compared against how studios price film work: price from a target of billable-equivalent hours plus direct costs plus overhead, with a revision cap and a paid extra-round fee. Sound: counting every hour not just the shoot day (the central insight, correct), amortising gear/software/insurance over bookings per year, a revision cap with a fee, second shooter as a cost rather than owner hours, processing fee applied to revenue including extra-round fees, minimum price algebra correct. Departures an accountant would flag: result is pre-tax profit with no self-employment tax (IRS Schedule SE, 15.3% on net earnings) or income tax, the hourly figure is therefore not take-home; no sales/VAT; overhead (office, marketing, unbillable inquiry and consultation time) is only partly captured through the single 'planning and admin' field; the gear-per-booking figure uses a user-chosen booking count, so it understates cost per booking for a slow year; no deposit or cash-flow timing. All limits except the first are not disclosed on the page.

defects.what: True hourly rate and profit are pre-tax and the results table does not say so; the disclaimer is only in the FAQ, so an owner can read $115/h as take-home (self-employment tax alone is 15.3% of net earnings)

Deliverable ladder discards the user's own ceremony and speeches edit hours and replaces highlight hours with the tier value, and uses the same shoot, travel and revision hours for every tier, so tiers are compared on a different job from the main report without saying so

Tests do not guard the edit-share warning boundary: changing '>= 0.5' to '> 0.5' passed 23 of 23; ladder profit/price values and sensitivity minimum prices are also unasserted, and the page tests only match strings in the HTML without running the script
canonical link, sitemap loc and robots Sitemap directive are relative ('./index.html'), which search engines ignore or reject
llms.txt points to the retired github.io host instead of marisstella.app
'Revision creep' text says 'about N hours of revisions' using revision hours for all rounds used, not only rounds past the cap

verdict: A small, honest, correct calculator: three bookings recompute exactly in an independent script and by hand, the minimum-price algebra round-trips, 23 of 23 tests pass, and two of three seeded arithmetic mutations were caught. It does not meet the bar because verification is only 2 (the warning-threshold mutation passed unnoticed and the page script is never executed by a test) and claims is 2 (stale github.io links in llms.txt, relative sitemap and canonical URLs, an unsourced 'two to four times' rule of thumb). A studio owner's accountant would accept the hour-counting and cost arithmetic but would ask for the pre-tax label and a tax-rate field before trusting 'true hourly rate' as what the owner keeps. Finished (completeness 3) but not at the bar. The page was not loaded in a browser during this audit.
